meta.name: SGLang vs vLLM on replayed agent traffic
meta.question: At equal hardware and identical agent traffic, does the serving engine (stock vLLM vs SGLang) change throughput and latency for this hybrid-attention model?
meta.domain: LLM serving for coding agents (no agents run; recorded traffic replayed)
meta.who_ran: Hamza Tahir (ZenML), with Claude Code agents
meta.harness_git_commit_note: `git log -1 --format=%H -- replay_bench.py serve_sglang.py`; bench.jsonl last committed in ec9420707285f3e778bbe9bd60a5b02cd1dc4464.
meta.code_location: the private research repo (paths at its root): replay_bench.py, serve_sglang.py, serve_vllm.py, bench.jsonl (repo root)
meta.total_spend_usd_note: Sum of the four records' `cost` in bench.jsonl: server up-time (startup + replay) x $3.95 per H100-hour. No sandboxes. Computed by replay_bench.py, not taken from the Modal bill; outside attempts.jsonl.

dataset.source: Recorded mini-swe-agent trajectories from this repo's own Terminal-Bench 2.0 runs at 32 agents with vLLM defaults (jobs/full*__mini-swe-agent__defaults__c32__*)
dataset.license_note: Derived from Terminal-Bench 2.0 task runs; license not recorded in the repo.
dataset.total_cases_note: 124 recorded sessions with 1,465 model turns (bench_vllm.log); turns whose recorded prompt exceeded 60,000 tokens were cut.
dataset.dropped_reason: None dropped; each run replays sessions in a fixed order until the 720 s window ends, so runs reach different numbers of sessions (see results[*].sessions_touched).

models_note: Served by us on one Modal H100 ('self-hosted' is outside the spec's two provider types); cost is GPU time at $3.95/h, not per token.

conditions.name: stock vLLM
conditions.description: vLLM 0.31.0, same flags as the agent study's defaults (serve_vllm.py COMMON), no extra args; one H100, 32 concurrent replayed sessions, 3 s gap between turns, 720 s replay window.

conditions.name: stock SGLang
conditions.description: SGLang 0.5.20 (lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.20) with the equivalent common flags, no extra args; one H100, 32 concurrent replayed sessions, 3 s gap between turns, 720 s replay window.

conditions.name: SGLang, lazy radix + bf16 states
conditions.description: SGLang with --mem-fraction-static 0.85, --mamba-radix-cache-strategy extra_buffer_lazy, --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16, --max-mamba-cache-size 128; one H100, 32 concurrent replayed sessions, 3 s gap between turns, 720 s replay window.

conditions.name: SGLang, radix cache off
conditions.description: SGLang with --mem-fraction-static 0.85, --disable-radix-cache, --max-mamba-cache-size 48; one H100, 32 concurrent replayed sessions, 3 s gap between turns, 720 s replay window.

setup.tools: None executed: each request re-sends the conversation exactly as the agent sent it before its i-th reply, with the bash tool schema, and asks for exactly as many tokens as the recorded reply (ignore_eos, temperature 0.6, streaming).

grading.judges_note: No accuracy: this measures serving only, so there is nothing to grade.

metrics.name: requests_completed
metrics.definition: requests that returned without error and with a usage block within the run.

metrics.name: generated_tokens_per_s
metrics.definition: completion tokens of completed requests / measured_window_s (the actual replay duration, which runs past 720 s while in-flight requests finish).

metrics.name: request_latency_p50_s / p90_s
metrics.definition: median / 90th percentile of request wall time over completed requests.

metrics.name: ttft_p50_s
metrics.definition: median time to the first streamed chunk.

metrics.name: running_requests_peak
metrics.definition: peak of the engine's running-requests gauge, scraped every 10 s.

noise.note: One run per setting; no repeats, so no run-to-run noise estimate or CIs. In the agent study, identical runs varied about 20% in time.

results_note: One entry per engine setting. n = requests sent; errored requests are counted in requests_errored and excluded from throughput and latency. Ratios vs stock vLLM are computed from the values shown.

failures.definition: Request failed with a connection reset from the server.
failures.example: A streamed request was reset by the SGLang server while the radix cache was off.

failures_note: Only the SGLang radix-cache-off run had errors; the other three runs had none.
replays_and_step_checks_note: No Kitaru replays. (The benchmark itself replays recorded traffic, but that is load generation, not a replay evaluation.)

headline_findings.finding: Stock SGLang completed 277 requests to stock vLLM's 504 on the same replayed traffic and H100.
Stock SGLang ran at most 5 requests at once for this hybrid model (its prefix cache reserves linear-attention state per request), so the rest queued.
Turning SGLang's radix cache off was its best setting tried, still behind stock vLLM in completed requests and generated tokens per second, with 11 connection resets.
Median request time was 27.92 s on stock vLLM and 88.09 s on stock SGLang.

limitations: One run per setting; no repeats or confidence intervals.
One model (a hybrid Gated DeltaNet + attention model, where SGLang's per-request linear-attention state is the bottleneck), one GPU type (H100), one workload (mini-swe-agent traffic at 32 sessions).
Only two non-default SGLang settings were tried, following its cookbook; not an exhaustive tuning of either engine.
Measures serving throughput and latency only, not agent outcomes.
Replay re-sends recorded prompts with fixed generation lengths (ignore_eos); real agents would react to slower responses (fewer turns per time limit).
Runs reached different numbers of sessions (39-55 of 124) within the window, so later sessions with longer prompts are weighted differently across engines.
Replayed prompts were a median 0.8769-0.9256 of the recorded prompt token counts (reasoning text is not re-sent), so prefix sharing is close to but not identical with the original run.
inconsistencies: FINDINGS.md section 10 says each replay ran 12 minutes; the recorded measured windows are 815.2-903.2 s (13.6-15.1 min), because in-flight requests finish after the 720 s deadline. Throughput is divided by the measured window.
FINDINGS.md says SGLang with radix cache off was '14% behind stock vLLM'; that matches completed requests (435 vs 504, ratio 0.8631); by generated tokens per second it is 0.8386 (16% behind).
FINDINGS.md section 10 does not mention the 11 errored requests (ConnectionResetError) in the radix-cache-off run.
FINDINGS.md says the claim tested against was 'SGLang about 50% faster than vLLM, measured on 3090s with a different model'; no source for that claim is recorded in the repo.
